official.description_text:
Researcher for teaching in Cognitive Interaction Design
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health
Job description
We are looking for a researcher for a 25% position during five months for teaching in course CH2010 Cognitive Interaction Design. This assignment will involve being the course leader for CH2010, ‘Cognitive Interaction Design’ which is a 7.5-credit course. This course typically has 30-40 students from the Masters of Technology, Work, and Health and the Masters of Sports Technology.
This assignment will include preparations for teaching, setting up the course webpage on the Canvas learning platform, delivering lectures and seminars, providing guidance and feedback on assignments, and conducting evaluations and examinations in accordance with the published ILOs and course content.
The work will take place at the KTH Flemingsberg campus with possibility for some digital work, following agreement from both parties.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree.
The applicant should have completed doctoral studies in: Ergonomics, Human Factors, Cognitive science, usability, or Product design.
You have pedagogic experience, including leading a course.
Oral and written fluency in English is required, since the course is offered in English.
As a person, you are collaborative with strong communication skills and you can also take initiative to accomplish goals independently. You have the ability to coordinate, manage, and lead a course independently.
Preferred qualifications
We prefer that you have experience teaching these topics: Ergonomics, Human Factors, Cognitive science, usability, or Product design. Ideally this teaching experience is in English and at the Masters level.
It is meritorious if you have experience using the Canvas learning management system (LMS).
It is meritorious if you have performed and published research in the areas of: Ergonomics, Human Factors, Cognitive science, usability, built environment, or Product design.
Knowledge of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Good knowledge of KTH education and administrative guidelines
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge. Please include a list of courses you have taught previously.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief letter describing why you want to teach cognitive interaction design, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long.
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid for a limited time according to the agreement - for up to five months, with access according to agreement.

ai.summary: A 25% five-month teaching-focused researcher position at KTH leading a Masters-level course in Cognitive Interaction Design for students in technology, work, and health domains. The role emphasizes course leadership, pedagogy, and independent course management rather than primary research contribution.

thematic_fit.rationale: Cognitive Interaction Design aligns with human-centred HCI and usability foundations. The course content domains (ergonomics, human factors, cognitive science, usability, product design) overlap with the researcher's spatial cognition and human-centred systems work. However, the posting does not signal immersive systems, collaboration, or learning science as course foci—these are inferred adjacencies rather than explicit alignment with the target identity's core themes.

methodological_fit.rationale: The researcher has user-studies and experimental-design skills that support HCI pedagogy and assessment. Academic writing experience suits course preparation and student feedback. However, the position is fundamentally a teaching assignment, not research leadership. No indication the role involves research supervision, lab work, or advancing the researcher's own spatial cognition and immersive learning agenda.

growth_value.rationale: Teaching at Masters level can deepen HCI pedagogy skills and expose the researcher to diverse student perspectives on interaction design. However, a five-month contract with no research leadership component offers limited opportunity to develop advanced statistical methods, physiological sensing, or eye-tracking capabilities that would strengthen future PhD applications. Growth is primarily pedagogical and institutional, not methodological.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a respected European technical institution and Sweden is a target country. A successful teaching record and publication in Swedish higher-education context can support future PhD candidacy. However, the limited contract duration (5 months, 25% FTE), lack of research funding or lab access, and absence of a supervisor relationship limit strategic value for PhD pathway development. The role is a teaching placement, not a research position.

eligibility_flags: Requires completed doctoral degree or equivalent; researcher holds MSc by Research in progress (thesis stage). Eligibility uncertain—posting explicitly requires 'completed doctoral studies' but does not clarify whether MSc by Research in final stage qualifies or whether only PhD/Dr. degrees are accepted.
Security clearance may apply if role is classified as security-sensitive; posting mentions Protective Security Act screening for certain positions but does not confirm this teaching post requires it.
Five-month limited contract with no stated research funding or lab allocation; no indication of continuation or pathway to permanent position.
risks: Eligibility risk: posting states 'doctoral degree or equivalent foreign degree' and 'completed doctoral studies in [fields]'—MSc by Research in progress may not satisfy this requirement. Contact KTH for clarification before investing effort.

Mismatch with PhD pathway: this is a teaching-focused contract, not a research position. It does not advance the researcher's own research agenda in immersive learning or spatial cognition, nor does it provide supervision, funding, or lab infrastructure typical of doctoral researcher or research-assistant-with-PhD-pathway roles.
Limited duration and FTE: five months at 25% capacity leaves minimal time to establish research presence or publication record in the institution.

Geographic fit is strong (Stockholm, Sweden); however, the position lacks the research intensity and supervisor relationship characteristic of target position types (doctoral-researcher, PhD-candidate, project-researcher).

eligibility_reasons: funding/salary not confirmed on the posting
